chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who visits the House (Kaaba) before shaving [his head], and he said: 'It is not proper except that he be excused due to forgetfulness.'

Then he said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was visited by some people on the Day of Sacrifice. Some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I sacrificed, and some said: I shaved before I threw [the pebbles]. They did not leave anything that they ought to have delayed except that they hastened it. So he said: 'There is no blame [on them].'

And it is from the Sunnah that a person eats from his sacrificial animal and feeds the beggar and the one who acknowledges [his need], according to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'So when their sides have settled, eat from them and feed the beggar and the one who acknowledges [his need].' This was narrated.

key_terms.اَلْمُعْتَرَّ: the one who acknowledges his need

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before sacrificing the animal during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that performing Hajj rituals out of sequence (Qada') incurs no penalty, a ruling derived from the Prophet’s lenient response to companions who rushed acts like shaving before sacrifice. It further establishes the Sunnah of distributing the sacrificial meat, linking the ritual to the Quranic command to feed both the needy and those who request food, thereby emphasizing social welfare alongside ritual correctness.
